title: Ranking All 20 Premier League Teams’ Performances on Matchday 6
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 12, 2026Bruno Fernandes (left), Florian Wirtz (center) and Erling Haaland all had differing weekends. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Fernandes, Wirtz), Michael Regan/Getty Images (Haaland)In this post-verdict world, Premier League points no longer have the same heft to them.

Manchester City currently lead the division with a faultless record from the first six games of the season, but what good will that do them if the independent commission dolls out a swingeing points deduction?

The tangible reward for City’s second-half romp through a crumbling Liverpool could soon be erased, but the quality of their performance, that strike from Erling Haaland, the ingenuity of Rayan Cherki, is crystallized in the moment.
On these shifting sands, everyone has to hold onto the few certainties there are.

It wasn’t a good day for Sunderland. / Oli SCARFF/AFP/Getty ImagesAny team stripped of their top scorer and talismanic defender is going to suffer but Régis Le Bris was rightly concerned by Sunderland’s distinct lack of “quality or composure” in possession. The Black Cats had 62% of the ball against a team so used to being the protagonist but came up short of ideas without Brian Brobbey to look for.

Marco Rose needs a win. / Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesBournemouth have played better than their meager points total of three, but they were never in danger of earning that elusive first win under Marco Rose at Stamford Bridge.“The last games we had some good performances,” the incoming manager admitted, “but today we struggled.”
If this was a clip from the Bundesliga it'd have 50k likes. pic.twitter.com/23QX4zKhlM

Manchester United have so many problems that people can get bogged down by the irrelevant ones.Rather than running statistics, Michael Carrick would be wise to dwell on how his collection of players (or strangers?) can look so woefully exposed against a Tottenham Hotspur side that started the game in 20th. Old Trafford has been a far more forgiving atmosphere than most grounds throughout the club’s 13 years of angst since Sir Alex Ferguson but even match-going fans are starting to lose their patience. Carrick has no defense, in a metaphorical or literal sense. “I understand the disappointment,” he shrugged, “the reality is what it is.”

The walls are closing in on Álvaro Arbeloa. / Justin Setterfield/Getty Images“Maybe you don’t know me,” an increasingly prickly Álvaro Arbeloa put it to a journalist this weekend, “but I played for the best team in world. I have coached the best team in the world. Maybe you don’t know, but just to let you know, that pressure is part of my life since I was a kid.”The former Real Madrid player and manager (for all of four months) is being subjected to a torrent of deserved pressure after another listless display and more dropped points.

Monday’s win offered Matthias Jaissle plenty of food for thought. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesAnother Monday night and another 4–1 thumping. Matthias Jaissle could be forgiven for channeling The Boomtown Rats but Newcastle’s hefty reverse against Coventry City was nowhere near as damning as their implosion at the hands of Leeds United in September.For large swathes of the weeknight clash, the Magpies had Coventry City on the ropes, creating a glut of chances they found creative ways to spurn. “The result is not what happened in the game,” Nico González fairly claimed. Yet, the backdoor was constantly left open during Newcastle’s attacking raids and the newly promoted hosts were in ruthless mood.

Liverpool collapsed after Ryan Gravenberch’s red card. / Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesPutting aside the mental gymnastics of what this result means in the grand context of the Premier League’s existence, this was an excellent game decided by the referee—as Andoni Iraola has been at pains to point out. For all Liverpool’s promise across that opening hour of numerical parity, the extent to which the Reds collapsed after Ryan Gravenberch’s dismissal cannot get lost in the fog of another refereeing controversy. Liverpool may have only had 10 players but they still collectively completed fewer passes than Cherki managed on his own across those final 30 minutes.
Another day at the office for Walter 😅 pic.twitter.com/LbP6mXgI2Z

Despite getting royally outplayed by their visitors, Crystal Palace’s players were still given a reward by the forgiving Pierre Sage. Sunday’s win ensured that they could have Monday off, sparking very loud festivities bursting out the locker room. Considering the roster were initially facing just a single rest day throughout the entirety of a busy October, some celebration is understandable—even if it wasn’t deserved.
https://t.co/IrHjItUkMl pic.twitter.com/egGdiN5hTx

One of the old clichés that David Moyes has fallen upon one or two times during his 1,202 matches of management is the need for a team to be at their best in both boxes. Well, Everton were guilty of two defensive blunders while Thierno Barry missed even more chances in the attacking penalty area. Against that backdrop, it’s impressive the Toffees were able to emerge with any points.
Some finish from Mo! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/RDHkGJ08Hr

Hull haven’t been declawed just yet. The Tigers have bolstered an unexpectedly bright start in the Premier League’s glamor ties with the kind of dogged battles for points which could be enough to evade a relegation the vast majority had predicted.Sergej Jakirović captured the mood of one point well earned on Sunday when he concluded: “Congratulations to both teams.”
Come for the goal, stay for John McGinn’s celebration 😅 pic.twitter.com/X8vYwvnaLf

Things are tentatively crawling in the right direction for Aston Villa, even if the sort of form which propelled them to fourth place last season is still some way off. As Unai Emery tellingly admitted: “We need to build the team.” Some vague semblance of structure looked a little clearer on Saturday.
